workedExamples.question:
Water flows into a tank at a rate of $r(t)$ litres per minute, where $r$ is increasing. Selected values are shown.

| $t$ (minutes) | 0 | 2 | 5 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $r(t)$ (litres/min) | 4 | 7 | 9 | 12 |

Use a left Riemann sum and a right Riemann sum with the three subintervals shown to approximate $\int_0^{10} r(t)\,dt$. State whether each is an over- or underestimate.
workedExamples.solution:
The widths are $2$, $3$ and $5$ minutes (not equal).

Left sum (heights at the left end of each subinterval):
$$2(4) + 3(7) + 5(9) = 8 + 21 + 45 = 74 \text{ litres}$$

Right sum (heights at the right end):
$$2(7) + 3(9) + 5(12) = 14 + 27 + 60 = 101 \text{ litres}$$

Since $r$ is increasing, each left rectangle sits below the graph and each right rectangle sits above it: $74$ litres is an underestimate and $101$ litres is an overestimate of the total water added.

workedExamples.question: Write $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(1 + \frac{2i}{n}\right)^2\frac{2}{n}$ as a definite integral and evaluate it.
workedExamples.solution:
Match to $\sum f(a + i\,\Delta x)\,\Delta x$: here $\Delta x = \frac{2}{n}$, so $b - a = 2$.

The input is $1 + \frac{2i}{n} = 1 + i\,\Delta x$, so $a = 1$, $b = 1 + 2 = 3$, and $f(x) = x^2$.

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(1 + \frac{2i}{n}\right)^2\frac{2}{n} = \int_1^3 x^2\,dx = \left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_1^3 = 9 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{26}{3}$$

(Equivalently $\int_0^2 (1 + x)^2\,dx = \frac{26}{3}$, taking $a = 0$ and $f(x) = (1 + x)^2$.)
